scams.name: Gohtong Jaya 'Wild Fish / Market Price' Seafood Bill-Shock at Genting Food Street
scams.description: Genting Highlands' most-documented 2026 overcharge anchor is the Gohtong Jaya seafood-restaurant 'market price / wild-caught' ambush, where unpriced 'specials' (steamed patin, grouper, lobster, abalone) land bills at RM 1,500–RM 2,500 on tour groups who never saw a price before ordering. The canonical press anchor is NST 'Genting Highlands restaurant under probe over RM 902 patin dish' (March 2026) — 13 Singaporean and Chinese tourists at Loong Kee Restaurant, Gohtong Jaya, were billed RM 902 for a 2.7 kg wild river patin at RM 338/kg; Malaysia's KPDN (Domestic Trade) opened a formal pricing-compliance probe. Mothership SG 'S'porean tourists get shock of their lives after Genting restaurant bill' (March 2026) and AsiaOne 'Singaporeans shocked to be charged S$290 for fish' (March 2026) document the same group. A separate Good Times / Shin Min Daily feature 'Tourists shocked after paying RM 1,762 at Gohtong Jaya restaurant' logs a second Singaporean family with a near-identical pattern. Community reports document the broader 'tourist tax' at Genting eateries, including a 2025 RM 120 overcharge for roti canai at nasi kandar and widespread complaints about Genting Highlands dining pricing. The 2026 mechanic: (a) a server waves tourists toward a wet tank or chiller of 'fresh / wild-caught' fish and quotes 'sikit mahal sahaja lah' (just a bit pricey) without producing a menu; (b) the fish is weighed AFTER it is killed and steamed — no reweigh opportunity; (c) the printed menu lists farmed patin at ~RM 60–RM 80/kg but 'wild patin buah' (river-caught) is written in pencil at RM 300–RM 400/kg; (d) side dishes, rice, Chinese tea, wet towels each add RM 8–RM 15; (e) a 10% service charge + 6% SST stack on top; (f) the bill is presented only after plates are cleared, with no itemized pre-order confirmation. For travelers: (1) BEFORE ordering anything, demand the printed menu with prices and photograph every page — if a server won't produce one, leave; (2) NEVER accept 'market price' or 'wild catch' without a written RM/kg quote AND an estimated weight confirmed in writing before the fish is killed; (3) if staff say 'we weigh after steaming', refuse — legitimate Malaysian seafood restaurants weigh live-in-front-of-you; (4) avoid 'wild patin buah', 'soon hock', 'patin sungai', grouper, abalone, or live prawn unless you personally watched the weigh-in; (5) order fixed-price rice-shop staples (claypot chicken rice, tau fu fah, Hakka noodles) if you want budget certainty — RM 15–RM 30 per person; (6) take photos of the menu price and the dish as it arrives — this is your evidence for a KPDN complaint at 1-800-886-800 or the ez-ADU app; (7) pay with a credit card so you can initiate a chargeback if overcharged per community reports; (8) if the bill is disputed, calmly ask for an itemized receipt and call tourist police at 03-2149 6590 before paying — Malaysian law requires visible pricing and a recipient like KPDN actively investigated Loong Kee after the March 2026 incident.
scams.avoidance: Demand printed menu with prices BEFORE ordering; photograph every page NEVER accept 'market price' / 'wild catch' without written RM/kg + estimated weight Skip wild patin buah, soon hock, grouper, abalone unless you watched live weigh-in Pay by credit card for chargeback leverage; photograph menu + dish as evidence KPDN hotline 1-800-886-800 or ez-ADU app for overcharge complaints
scams.location: Gohtong Jaya food street (Loong Kee Restaurant, Jalan Lau Ko Lin), SkyAvenue mall casual-dining zone, First World Plaza seafood stalls, Chin Swee Caves Temple roadside restaurants, Resorts World Genting Chinese fine-dining outlets

scams.name: Fake Genting SkyWorlds Theme Park Tickets & QR-Code Reseller Scam
scams.description: Genting SkyWorlds Theme Park tickets are Malaysia's most-impersonated attraction inventory — fake QR codes, cloned websites, and 'discount reseller' posts on Facebook Marketplace, Shopee, Lazada, and Carousell produce thousands of turned-away tourists at the SkyWorlds gate each year. The MOTAC (Ministry of Tourism, Arts & Culture) #TakNakScam campaign and Resorts World Genting's rwgenting.com/en/daily-notice/fake-websites-alert.html page (updated 13 December 2024) are the regulatory anchors. Resorts World Genting has posted repeated public advisories via Facebook and an Instagram reel 'Stay Safe, Stay Smart' warning of 'unauthorised resellers offering Resorts World Genting rooms / tickets' that lead to 'scams, lost money, or even getting kicked out of your room'. The Genting SkyWorlds Facebook page post 'You know what's not fake news — Buy 1 Free 1 tickets' explicitly warns against QR codes 'given in comment sections' and named fake 'Shawn Mendes / promo' ticket scam crossovers. Community reports document the 'too-good-to-be-true discount' warnings and emphasize the importance of booking tickets on DATE-SPECIFIC official channels to avoid counterfeit vouchers. The 2025–2026 mechanic: (a) Facebook Marketplace / WhatsApp / Carousell posts offering SkyWorlds day passes at RM 80–RM 120 (vs. RM 183 adult gate / RM 155 online official) with 'urgent sale — can't go, already paid'; (b) seller sends a PDF ticket or QR-code screenshot — either already-scanned (single-use), a photoshopped fake, or issued under a different person's name that fails gate-ID match; (c) fake cloned websites using Genting-like domains (gentinghotel-resort.com, rwgenting-booking.com, gentingresort.com.my) that take card payment but issue no real ticket; (d) 'promo code' comment-section replies on official SkyWorlds Facebook posts linking to phishing pages that capture card and OTP; (e) scalpers at SkyAvenue mall entry selling printed 'unused' tickets that were bought with stolen cards and get cancelled by 4 PM; (f) fake 'official partner' WhatsApp numbers claiming Klook/KKday clearance. For travelers: (1) book SkyWorlds tickets ONLY via the official URL www.gentingskyworlds.com or www.rwgenting.com, or via verified aggregators Klook and KKday with explicit 'Genting SkyWorlds Theme Park Official' listing badge; (2) refuse every Facebook Marketplace, Carousell, Shopee, Lazada, or WhatsApp 'private sale' — there are zero legitimate reseller scenarios for same-day tickets; (3) verify domain spelling — the ONLY legitimate domains are rwgenting.com and gentingskyworlds.com (no hyphens, no -booking suffix); (4) check the QR code by loading the buyer's confirmation email header — it must come from @rwgenting.com or @gentingskyworlds.com; (5) pay by credit card on the official site so chargebacks are possible if tickets fail at the gate; (6) NEVER scan a QR code posted in a comment section or sent by a stranger on WhatsApp; (7) keep screenshots of every transaction + the MOTAC #TakNakScam hotline 1-300-88-5050 for immediate complaint if refused at the gate; (8) if scammed, file a report at the SkyAvenue Auxiliary Police counter AND lodge a complaint via Malaysia's NSRC (National Scam Response Centre) 997 within 24 hours to freeze fraudulent transactions.
scams.avoidance: Book SkyWorlds tickets ONLY at gentingskyworlds.com, rwgenting.com, Klook, or KKday Refuse every Facebook / Carousell / WhatsApp / Shopee 'private sale' or 'discount reseller' Verify email is @rwgenting.com or @gentingskyworlds.com; pay by credit card NEVER scan QR codes posted in comments or sent by strangers NSRC hotline 997 within 24 hours if scammed; MOTAC #TakNakScam 1-300-88-5050
scams.location: Genting SkyWorlds Theme Park main gate, SkyAvenue mall ticket counter, First World Plaza concourse, online (Facebook Marketplace, Carousell, Shopee, Lazada), Awana SkyWay lower terminal

scams.name: Resorts World Genting Fake 'Hotel Staff' Room-Phone & OTP/Card-Verification Fraud
scams.description: Resorts World Genting maintains an active fraud-alert ecosystem specifically because fake 'hotel staff' phone scams targeting First World Hotel, Genting Grand, Resorts World Awana, and Crockfords Hotel guests are a continuous problem. The regulatory anchor is rwgenting.com/en/daily-notice/keep-your-data-safe-from-fraudulent-activity.html, which states in the resort's own words: 'Resorts World Genting will never call you to obtain your OTP or password for any reason.' The Instagram reel 'Stay Safe, Stay Smart' and Facebook advisory posts by @ResortsWorldGenting warn repeatedly about fake card-verification calls, fraudulent booking websites (gentinghotel-resort.com, rwgenting-booking.com family), and fake OTP-phishing SMS blasts; The Star 'MCMC shuts down illegal transceiver station used to send scam messages in Genting' (January 2026) confirms the telco-side interception of phishing SMS batches targeting Genting guests. Community reports document adjacent fraud patterns around used keycards and fake room-resellers. The 2025–2026 mechanic: (a) an in-room telephone rings soon after check-in — caller claims 'front desk, your card was declined, can you confirm the card number and CVV to re-verify?'; (b) SMS or WhatsApp arrives shortly after booking, posing as 'Resorts World Reservations — please click this link to confirm your stay / pay a re-confirmation fee'; (c) fake booking sites (gentinghotel-resort.com, rwgenting-resort.com, genting-booking.net) take full card details, issue no reservation, and the traveler arrives to find no record at check-in; (d) 'unauthorised resellers' on Facebook/Carousell sell used keycards or 'member free nights' that are cancelled by 4 PM the first day, locking guests out; (e) in-casino adjuncts — strangers in SkyCasino ask to 'borrow your Genting Rewards card for a moment to top up' then skim. Community reports are explicit: 'Beware of mainland chinese scammers' operating both begging and card-lift layers around the casino floor. For travelers: (1) NEVER give card number, CVV, OTP, or password over the hotel room phone — legitimate front desk NEVER asks for payment re-verification by phone; if asked, hang up and walk to the front desk in person; (2) book rooms ONLY on rwgenting.com (exact URL, no hyphens) or verified aggregators Agoda, Booking.com, Trip.com; (3) ignore every 'confirmation fee', 're-activation link', or 'pay deposit to avoid cancellation' SMS — Resorts World never charges beyond the original reservation; (4) refuse 'cheap member room' offers on Facebook / WhatsApp — these are either used keycards or outright impersonations; (5) on arrival at First World Hotel, confirm your room number only at the front desk counter — never announce it in the lobby within earshot of strangers; (6) never hand your Genting Rewards card to anyone at a slot machine or table — the card links to stored e-Cash and points that can be drained; (7) if scammed, call Resorts World Auxiliary Police in-resort via +603-2718 1118 (main line), then Malaysia's NSRC at 997 within 24 hours to freeze the fraudulent transaction; (8) keep the URL bookmarked — every official advisory lives under rwgenting.com/en/daily-notice/.
scams.avoidance: NEVER give card / CVV / OTP / password over hotel room phone; walk to front desk Book rooms ONLY at rwgenting.com (no hyphens) or Agoda/Booking.com/Trip.com Ignore every 'confirmation fee' SMS; Resorts World never charges beyond reservation Refuse 'cheap member room' Facebook/WhatsApp offers — keycards get cancelled by 4 PM NSRC 997 within 24 hours; Resorts World Auxiliary Police +603-2718 1118
scams.location: First World Hotel, Genting Grand Hotel, Resorts World Awana, Crockfords Hotel, SkyAvenue check-in lobby, online (fake booking domains), Facebook Marketplace, WhatsApp / SMS phishing

scams.name: SkyCasino Distraction Chip-Lift & Casino-Floor Begging-Syndicate Scam
scams.description: Genting's SkyCasino floor hosts a documented distraction-and-lift ecosystem operated by organized foreign syndicates, overlaid with a casino-floor begging layer that targets older Singaporean and mainland-Chinese gamblers. The 2025 press anchor is AsiaOne / Stomp 'S'porean couple says they were scammed at Genting Highlands casino after buying food for women posing as beggars' (May 2025), which logs the May 7, 2025 arrest of four foreign nationals at Resorts World Genting for organized begging-and-scam activity. One first-person account describes the Sic Bo table team-of-three distraction-lift pattern: 'Chinese nationals mainly executed this scam at Sic Bo table — in a team of 3s, one distracts while the others lift chips.' Community reports also document a viral-video variant targeting the elderly and a 2025 community warning: 'Beware of mainland chinese scammers.' Travelers document the SkyCasino environment shift: 'I've been going to Genting Highlands sky casino for over 2 years; back then it was 1–2 people who would quietly ask to exchange.' Community reports also log a parallel loan-shark approach pattern at Resorts World Genting. The Malaysian Immigration arrest of 152 foreign nationals for Genting-adjacent scam syndicates (The Star, April 2025) provides the enforcement anchor. The 2025–2026 mechanic: (a) a friendly stranger joins your slot-machine bank or table, chats about 'lucky numbers / lucky machines', leans across your tray; (b) a second accomplice bumps past, covering the tray with a jacket or plastic bag; (c) chips / Genting Rewards card / phone are palmed; (d) women on the casino floor approach with 'I lost all my money, can you buy me food' — sympathy extraction pattern with S'porean-targeting playbook per AsiaOne coverage; (e) 'money-counting helper' strangers offer to count cash for new gamblers and short-count RM 50–RM 200; (f) loan-shark adjuncts offer 'cash for chips' at 2:1 markup then demand 10x repayment; (g) the Dec 2024 AsiaOne 'hypnotist gang' warning documents an elderly-targeted variant involving distraction-to-theft. For travelers: (1) treat every chatty stranger at a slot machine or table as a potential team member — politely move if anyone sits beside you and starts conversation; (2) NEVER leave chips unattended on a tray, even briefly — stack them in your dominant-hand pocket when stepping away; (3) NEVER hand your Genting Rewards card to anyone — it carries stored e-Cash; (4) refuse every 'please buy me food / I lost all my money' approach — the May 2025 arrests prove these are syndicated; (5) decline every loan-shark 'cash for chips' offer — this is illegal in Malaysia and the 'lenders' operate via threats; (6) use the cashier cage (not casino-floor strangers) to exchange; keep only one day's bankroll in pocket, rest in hotel safe; (7) report suspicious approaches to Auxiliary Police on the casino floor immediately; (8) if chips go missing, request CCTV review via the Pit Boss — Genting has comprehensive coverage.
scams.avoidance: Treat chatty slot-neighbors as potential teams; move if someone sits beside you NEVER leave chips unattended; stack in dominant-hand pocket when stepping away Refuse every 'buy me food / lost all my money' approach — they are syndicated Never hand Genting Rewards card to anyone; use cashier cage only, not strangers Auxiliary Police on casino floor for suspicious approaches; CCTV review via Pit Boss
scams.location: SkyCasino main floor, Casino de Genting (original casino), Sic Bo tables, slot-machine banks, First World Plaza casino concourse, SkyAvenue mall food court entry points

scams.name: KL–Genting Unlicensed Shuttle-Van 'Souvenir Stop' & Upsell Scam
scams.description: The KL-to-Genting corridor is saturated with unlicensed shuttle-van operators who intercept tourists at Bukit Bintang, KLCC, and KL Sentral hotels with 'day trip' offers priced 2–3x the official Genting Express fare (RM 10–RM 20 one-way from KL Sentral terminal per rwgenting.com/en/getting-here/express-bus.html), then layer detours at commission-paying 'souvenir stops', chocolate factories, and Bentong-area batik shops. The JPJ (Road Transport Department) enforcement pattern is documented in The Star / NST reporting on unlicensed tourist van sweeps. Community reports confirm: 'Genting Resort World Express Bus service — max price is RM 20 for adults, and lowest fare is RM 12 for senior citizens; this includes the Awana SkyWay.' Travelers document the same safe-route pattern across 2024-2025. The broader KLIA tout-overcharge pattern (Malay Mail 'Woman to be charged over KLIA taxi scam — RM 836 for illegal KLIA taxi ride', and CariCarz.my 'KLIA tout arrested after RM 800 tourist scam' 2025) maps the JPJ enforcement environment. The 2025–2026 mechanic: (a) a 'tour operator' approaches in Bukit Bintang hotel lobbies offering 'KL–Genting day trip RM 120 per person, includes cable car'; (b) the van makes 2–4 unscheduled 'souvenir stops' at Bentong batik factories, chocolate outlets, or durian farms where the driver earns 10–20% commission on guest purchases; (c) the 'included' cable-car ticket turns out to be an upsell — driver demands an additional RM 40–RM 60 at Awana; (d) vans are often unlicensed (no JPJ commercial permit), uninsured for passengers, and driven by drivers without a PSV license — the June 2024 AsiaOne report on a Genting Highlands tour-bus fatality involved exactly this 'driver didn't have license' pattern; (e) return-trip pickup is often 'delayed' until after pressure-purchase stops; (f) fake 'tourism agent' cards / WhatsApp contacts posing as Malaysia Tourism Board partners per the MITTA/MOTAC 2025 Travel Scam Alert. For travelers: (1) use the OFFICIAL Genting Express bus from KL Sentral Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS) or Terminal Bersepadu Gombak (TBG) — RM 10 one-way (RM 7 for Rewards members), RM 20 return with Awana SkyWay cable car included; tickets at rwgenting.com/en/getting-here/express-bus.html OR in person at the KL Sentral Aerobus counter; (2) Grab / MyCar rideshare KL–Genting is RM 120–RM 180 one-way for the whole vehicle, not per person — compare before accepting a 'tour' pitch; (3) refuse every hotel-lobby 'tour van' offer — legitimate agencies require a MOTAC tourism license number, verifiable at motac.gov.my/semakan; (4) NEVER pay the driver cash before departure; pay on arrival at destination when possible; (5) explicitly refuse all 'souvenir stops' — say 'direct to Genting / direct to KL' when boarding and get it written on the receipt; (6) if offered a 'package' with cable-car ticket bundled, buy SkyWay separately online (RM 10 standard gondola, RM 50 glass-floor) to confirm real pricing; (7) use Easybook, BusOnlineTicket, or RedBus for verified operators (Aerobus, Genting Express, Cititrans); (8) in emergencies call JPJ hotline 1-800-88-7723 or tourist police 03-2149 6590.
scams.avoidance: Use OFFICIAL Genting Express bus from KL Sentral or TBS: RM 10 one-way, RM 20 return with cable car Grab / MyCar KL–Genting is RM 120–RM 180 per vehicle, not per person — compare first Refuse every hotel-lobby 'tour van'; verify agency at motac.gov.my/semakan Explicitly refuse 'souvenir stops' — get 'direct route' written on receipt JPJ 1-800-88-7723 or tourist police 03-2149 6590
scams.location: KL Sentral Aerobus Genting Express terminal, Bukit Bintang hotel lobbies, KLCC pickup points, Terminal Bersepadu Selatan (TBS), Terminal Bersepadu Gombak (TBG), Bentong toll plaza souvenir-stop layover, Awana SkyWay lower terminal

scams.name: ATM DCC 'Home-Currency Conversion' Markup at Resorts World & Gohtong Jaya
scams.description: Resorts World Genting and Gohtong Jaya are dense with Maybank, CIMB, Public Bank, RHB, and OCBC Malaysia ATMs, and the vast majority prompt foreign-card users with a dynamic-currency-conversion (DCC) 'would you like to pay in your home currency?' offer — a built-in 3–10% markup that bypasses the traveler's bank FX rate. Community reports describe DCC: 'DCC is a scam where if you are using a credit card in a foreign country, they'll offer to do the exchange rate conversion for you — the operator (not your bank) sets the exchange rate, which typically includes a 3–7 % markup over the real rate.' Wise, Visa Malaysia, and mexc.com/news 'Malaysia ATM Withdrawal Guide' confirm the 2.5–3.5% FX fee plus potential DCC markup pattern on top. The Malaysia-Safe community safety advisory (malaysiasafe.app/safety/scams/dynamic-currency-conversion) logs the pattern specifically for inbound tourists: 'If you accept, the ATM operator sets the exchange rate, which typically includes a 3–7 % markup; on a RM 1,000 withdrawal that is RM 30–RM 70 extra.' For USD / SGD / AUD / GBP / EUR cardholders the effective withdrawal markup at Genting ATMs frequently hits 8–12% (DCC + operator + issuer foreign-transaction fee stacking). Beyond DCC, community reports warn about casino-floor 'money-counting helper' strangers who short-count cash after an ATM withdrawal — an adjacent layer. The 2025–2026 mechanic: (a) traveler inserts a foreign Visa/Mastercard at a First World Plaza, SkyAvenue, or Gohtong Jaya ATM; (b) screen prompts 'Convert to USD? Rate 1 USD = 4.72 MYR' (interbank rate ~4.25; markup ~11%) with 'Accept / Decline' buttons styled to favor 'Accept'; (c) a RM 1,000 withdrawal locks in USD 235.85 instead of the ~USD 212 the card's network rate would have delivered; (d) a separate 'convenience fee' of RM 12–RM 24 layers on top; (e) post-ATM approach by 'friendly' helpers offering to count cash; (f) at POS terminals in SkyAvenue restaurants and Genting Premium Outlets, foreign cards get the same DCC prompt — often defaulted to 'home currency' by staff pressing 'Yes' before handing the PIN pad over. For travelers: (1) at every ATM in Genting, REFUSE 'conversion to home currency' / 'pay in USD/SGD' — always press 'Decline conversion' or 'Continue in MYR' to let YOUR bank set the rate; (2) if the screen does not offer a decline option (rare), cancel and use a different ATM; (3) use Maybank or CIMB ATMs inside physical bank branches when possible — these typically have the most transparent prompts; (4) at POS card terminals (restaurants, SkyAvenue shops, Genting Premium Outlets), watch the screen and INSIST on 'Pay in MYR' — if staff say 'home currency is standard', decline and ask the terminal be reset; (5) bring a no-FX-fee card (Wise, Revolut, Chase Sapphire, Charles Schwab Debit) for the best Genting rates; (6) carry some cash exchanged at a KL Bukit Bintang money changer before arrival — Genting-area rates are 3–5% worse; (7) set real-time transaction alerts on your banking app to catch hidden DCC markups immediately; (8) NEVER accept a stranger's help counting cash after a withdrawal — per 2025 community reports this is the casino-begging crew layer.
scams.avoidance: REFUSE 'home-currency' / 'pay in USD/SGD' prompt — always 'Continue in MYR' Use Maybank or CIMB ATMs inside physical bank branches for transparent prompts At POS, watch screen + insist on 'Pay in MYR'; decline if staff default to home currency Bring a no-FX-fee card (Wise, Revolut, Chase Sapphire, Charles Schwab) Exchange cash at KL Bukit Bintang money changer — Genting rates are 3–5% worse
scams.location: First World Plaza Maybank / CIMB / Public Bank ATMs, SkyAvenue mall Maybank & OCBC ATMs, Gohtong Jaya 7-Eleven and bank-branch ATMs, Genting Premium Outlets RHB ATM, Awana SkyWay lower terminal ATM
